claims.value: The prior durable architecture was a modular backbone-and-spurs network with a protected core hub, distributed production cells/mining outposts, single-item rail lanes and buffers, and measured upgrades instead of a monolithic mega-base.

The new requirement is one Constructorizer plus two Facturers while every Base Core stays level 0. A level-0 core has 1,000 heat capacity; the machines consume 500, 650, and 650 heat. Constructorizer + Facturer = 1,150, and two Facturers = 1,300, so every possible heavy-machine pair exceeds one core’s capacity. Their aggregate heat is 1,800, but protection is constrained independently at each occupied core rather than by an aggregate pool.

The safe revision uses three occupied level-0 cores: Constructorizer cell A starts at 500/1,000 heat with 500 remaining; Facturer cells B and C each start at 650/1,000 with 350 remaining. Inputs, outputs, power, logistics, storage, and defenses must fit inside each cell’s remaining allowance, and no construction may proceed if the complete measured site total would exceed 1,000. Amplifier claims are excluded from the arithmetic until verified in-game.

Before construction, verify in the current Update 1 build menu that the three heavy machines and every proposed support component are actually unlocked, then record each core’s existing load and calculate the complete per-site total. Build the three cells independently only after all totals are safe; use only confirmed Update 1 equipment and exclude hidden content, future Rail v.4/v.5, and pre-Update-1 guidance.

Assign exactly one heavy machine to each of three level-0 occupied cores; do not treat unused capacity at one core as available to another.

Do not credit Base Core Amplifiers in the initial budget because their documented capacity values conflict with underlying temperature data.
Preserve Update 1 authority: use only components confirmed in the live build/unlock menus; exclude hidden equipment, future Rail v.4/v.5, and outdated playtest guidance.

answer.answer: Straylight is advanced to an implementation-ready child state at revision rev_000002_7323ec9a8a69. The first build is a persistent, snapshot-pinned typed workspace API; the historical token figures remain regression observations and are not an apples-to-apples architecture verdict.

claims.value: Straylight is an agent-first, portable context and durable-work layer that preserves both learned knowledge and the live, provenance-bearing state needed to resume and advance work; Markdown and Obsidian are prototype and projection formats, not the product boundary.

The historical one-shot result of about 1,070 mean estimated tokens versus 2,932 for the workspace was a retrieval-only regression observation, not proof that the workspace architecture failed or should remain a BM25 shell. The implementation evaluation must report cumulative cached replay separately from uncached input, so the old aggregate comparison cannot serve as an apples-to-apples API efficiency verdict.

The first persistent build slice is a snapshot-pinned typed workspace API that reopens a revision-N parent checkpoint, refreshes to N+1 with an inspectable diff, supports batched query/read operations over exact and lexical retrieval plus a pluggable semantic path, and atomically commits an immutable child checkpoint carrying its parent identity and source references without reconstructing the complete prior corpus.

The transition gate passes only when each harness case completes in at most four workspace calls, reproduces the answer claims obtained through direct filesystem access, demonstrates N-to-N+1 checkpoint refresh and diff exposure, emits a source-preserving immutable child linked to its parent, and reports cumulative cached replay and uncached input separately.
